description: React (Vite + TypeScript) SPA: Cognito auth flows (signup, email verification, login, logout, token refresh, forgot/reset password) using amazon-cognito-identity-js with a PUBLIC app client (no secret); DB connection manager UI; SQL editor with live (debounced) syntax + schema validation; results panel (syntax errors, schema errors, warnings); original-vs-suggested query comparison with explanation; copy/export. An authenticated API client attaches the Cognito access token and refreshes it. Must build with zero TypeScript errors.
steps: Scaffold frontend/ with Vite React+TS: package.json (react, react-dom, react-router-dom, amazon-cognito-identity-js, @monaco-editor/react or CodeMirror for the SQL editor, axios), devDeps (typescript, vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, @types/*, eslint, prettier). Add tsconfig.json (strict), vite.config.ts (dev proxy /api -> http://localhost:8000), index.html, src/main.tsx, src/App.tsx with react-router routes.

Create src/config.ts reading Vite env vars (VITE_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID, VITE_COGNITO_APP_CLIENT_ID, VITE_AWS_REGION, VITE_API_BASE_URL). Create src/auth/cognito.ts wrapping amazon-cognito-identity-js: signUp, confirmSignUp (email code), resendCode, signIn, signOut, getSession (with automatic refresh), forgotPassword, confirmForgotPassword. No client secret used.

Create src/auth/AuthContext.tsx (React context + provider) exposing user, tokens, and the auth methods; a RequireAuth route guard that redirects to /login. Create auth pages under src/pages/auth/: SignUp, ConfirmSignUp, Login, ForgotPassword, ResetPassword, plus logout action.

Create src/api/client.ts: axios instance with baseURL from config, request interceptor attaching the current Cognito access token (refreshing via getSession when near expiry), response interceptor redirecting to /login on 401. Typed functions: testConnection, getSchema, validateSql, optimizeSql matching backend api_models.

Create src/pages/ConnectionManager.tsx: form to enter DB connection (dialect select postgres/mysql/sqlserver/sqlite/oracle, host, port, db, user, password, optional 'enable data sampling' toggle, sensitive-columns-to-exclude field). Calls testConnection + getSchema; shows connection status and a schema tree (tables -> columns/indexes). Password field never persisted to localStorage.

Create src/pages/Analyzer.tsx: the main workspace. SQL editor component (src/components/SqlEditor.tsx) with debounced onChange (~400ms) that calls validateSql for live syntax + schema validation; a ResultsPanel (src/components/ResultsPanel.tsx) rendering syntax_errors, schema_errors, warnings with severity styling; an 'Analyze & Optimize' button calling optimizeSql; a ComparisonView (src/components/ComparisonView.tsx) showing original vs suggested SQL side by side with the explanation, the optimization list, the serving provider, an is_suggestion_valid badge, a performance-estimate disclaimer, and Copy + Export (download .sql) actions. Show a clear 'AI temporarily unavailable' notice when ai_available is false while still showing syntax/schema results.
Add src/index.css / basic layout + a top nav showing the logged-in user and logout. Keep styling lightweight (plain CSS or a small CSS file), no heavy UI dependency required.

Add frontend/.eslintrc + prettier config; ensure `npm install` then `npm run build` (tsc + vite build) completes with zero type errors. Add a couple of lightweight Vitest tests for pure helpers (e.g. token-near-expiry logic, export filename builder) if quick, but the build passing is the required gate.
acceptance_criteria: `cd frontend && npm install && npm run build` completes with zero TypeScript errors and produces dist/
All six auth flows exist and are wired to amazon-cognito-identity-js with a public app client (no secret in code)
SQL editor triggers debounced live validation and the results panel renders syntax errors, schema errors, and warnings distinctly

Comparison view shows original vs suggested SQL, explanation, provider, validity badge, performance-estimate disclaimer, and copy/export; AI-unavailable state is handled without hiding syntax/schema results
The API client attaches the Cognito access token and handles 401 by redirecting to login; DB password is never written to localStorage
verification: cd frontend && npm install && npm run build
